name: 張文中
objective:
Modern control theory mainly focuses on linear system analysis and design.  This is the course where students from a variety of backgrounds begin to acquire the mathematical tools used in research literature involving linear systems.  The core material covered in this course is the theory of time-varying linear systems, in both continuous-time and discrete-time, with frequent specialization to the time invariant case.
The goals of the course can be summarized as below:
	Learning some useful facts about linear systems, emphasizing motivation and significance rather than mathematical formalism.
	Learning some useful facts from matrix theory and linear algebra, and seeing them used.
	Learning about mathematical reasoning.
The course is presented in a standard format of lectures and readings sets.  In addition to the closed-book final examination, there will be a number of homework assignments equally spaced over the term.  You will be asked to do selected homework questions during class hours for evaluation purpose.  Each student is required to make a presentation and submit a report based on a technical paper in related topics.  The lecture will be based mainly, but not entirely, on material in the textbook.  Course-related information will mainly be distributed via emails.  Please make sure to keep us updated about your email addresses.
